title: Hole Patterns
alignmentHeadline: Reduce forced bends and fatigue risks
intro: We normally simulate spoke directions from the hub drawing and lacing, then match four drilling angles to bring the nipple axis closer to the designed tension line, reducing extra bending moments and seat side loading.
openVideo: Play automated angled rim drilling video
videoCaption: Automated angled drilling · Watch the machining process

axialCapability.label: Axial angles for the hub flanges
axialCapability.description: Set each side's axial drilling angle to match the distance from the hub center plane to its flange.

longitudinalCapability.label: Longitudinal angles for the lacing
longitudinalCapability.description: Set the two longitudinal drilling angles to match flange PCD, hole count and the lacing pattern.

alignmentPrinciple.title: Designed to avoid forced bends
alignmentPrinciple.description: Match two axial and two longitudinal angles together to reduce forced bending at the nipple exit and bring tension transfer closer to coaxial alignment.
alignmentPrinciple.manufacturingLimit: Avoiding forced bends is a geometric design goal. Drawing dimensions, machining and assembly tolerances still affect the finished fit; exact coaxial alignment is not guaranteed.

hubDrawingGeometry.title: Simulate geometry from the hub drawing
hubDrawingGeometry.description: We normally use drawing dimensions for WL / WR, left/right flange PCD and spoke exits, together with rim ERD, hole positions and lacing, to model spoke directions in space.

matchedDrillingAngles.title: Match four drilling angles
matchedDrillingAngles.description: Match two axial and two longitudinal drilling angles to the simulated spoke directions, minimizing forced bends in the design. Drawing revision, hole mapping and the machining plan are confirmed directly.

manufacturingAndAssemblyTolerances.title: Account for manufacturing and assembly tolerances
manufacturingAndAssemblyTolerances.description: Drawing dimensions have tolerances, and actual hubs, rim molding, drilling and assembly also vary. Nominal dimensions in the simulation cannot be treated as identical to the finished fit.

carbonRimInterior.title: Limits of the molded carbon rim interior
carbonRimInterior.description: The internal nipple seats of a closed carbon rim are formed during molding and cannot be trued by CNC turning around the full internal circumference. Even a smooth interior has local surface variation that affects nipple contact. Custom drilling can closely match the drawing geometry, but cannot also remove interior variation or assembly deviations.

angleAlignmentBenefits.title: Reduce fatigue risks at three load-critical points
angleAlignmentBenefits.misalignmentExplanation: When fixed drilling angles do not match the actual hub and lacing, tension can force the nipple to tilt and the spoke to bend at its thread transition. This extra bending and side loading can contribute to nipple-seat cracking and spoke fatigue failure.

spokeEndFatigue.mechanism: Less forced bending and extra bending moment
spokeEndFatigue.title: Lower spoke thread-root failure risk
spokeEndFatigue.description: Reduce additional bending stress at the spoke thread transition, lowering the risk of local fatigue and breakage under repeated loads.

nippleSideLoading.title: Less nipple side loading and damage
nippleSideLoading.description: Let the nipple follow the spoke's load direction more freely, reducing tilt, one-sided loading and local deformation.

rimHoleLocalDamage.mechanism: Less seat side loading and stress concentration
rimHoleLocalDamage.title: Lower carbon rim nipple-seat cracking risk
rimHoleLocalDamage.description: Reduce lateral nipple pressure against the hole wall and seat edge, limiting local stress concentrations and fatigue damage.

angleAlignmentBenefits.assemblyContext: Angle matching works together with suitable nipples, washers where specified by the design, and correct wheel-building tension.

symmetrical.label: Symmetrical axial angles
symmetrical.description: For wheels with similar hub geometry and lacing on both sides.

asymmetrical.label: Independent left/right axial angles
asymmetrical.description: Match each flange direction separately when WL / WR differ.

angled.label: Longitudinal lacing angles
angled.description: Match drilling angles in the longitudinal plane to radial or crossed lacing.

customization.title: Custom hub and lacing compatibility
customization.intro: Share your hub drawing, hub and rim models, and intended lacing so we can confirm the drilling plan with you directly.

commitment.title: Automated machining and consistency
commitment.body: Our self-developed automated machinery controls consistency in hole placement and axis direction, enabling repeatable production of custom drilling patterns.
